Subject: Request: retention carveout & backup purge timeline

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Riverbend's security team has a couple of follow-ups specific to the PHI-adjacent dataset we'll be routing through Redwood for inference. Two asks we need to align on before Legal will sign:

1) Can you confirm the backup purge timeline for customer snapshots and object-store backups that contain derived logs/metadata? Our security policy requires a 60-day maximum for backups containing PHI unless a documented exception is in place.

2) We need a small carveout for forensics logs (only triggered by incident) — ideally encrypted and retained for 180 days with strict access controls and audit logs.

3) Please provide the current subprocessors list and an indication of which subprocessors have access to backups or persistent snapshots.

If you can share a redlined DPA amendment or a proposed retention matrix, that will move this along on our side. We can do a sync tomorrow afternoon if helpful.

Much appreciated —
Li Zhang
Security & Privacy Lead, Riverbend Health

Li/Vanessa — looping in Legal. Thanks for the detailed asks; high level we can proceed but want to note a couple negotiated controls we typically include in a DPA amendment:

- 60-day purge window for backups that are known to contain PHI-derived content (this will be defined in the amendment by dataset ID and a retained-data tag).
- Forensic exception: 180 days max, access only by named security contacts with 2FA + privileged access logs exported to an immutable audit store.
- Subprocessor visibility: we'll list all subprocessors and mark which have backup/persistent snapshot access. QuantumCloud (object storage) and EdgeGPU Systems (serving cache snapshots) are the two who will need to be explicitly named in the amendment.
- Evidence: we will include a runbook excerpt and an example backup purge log that shows the TTL enforcement cadence and deletion confirmation hashes (we'll redact the hashes in shared copies).

I have redlined the DPA PDF attached — if you agree on the language, we'll prepare a DocuSign amendment referencing the dataset IDs. A few operational notes for Karthik: please confirm whether the 60-day purge is compatible with our current snapshot retention policy for dedicated pools vs hosted buckets.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_dpa_v2_marked.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Li Zhang <l.zhang@riverbend-health.org>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: retention carveout & backup purge timeline

Quick operational confirmation from Security/Compliance:

- Snapshot and backup topology: Riverbend production runs on dedicated pools for inference artifacts (snapshots taken hourly, full backups twice weekly). Backups are stored in QuantumCloud object storage; snapshots for serving state are replicated to EdgeGPU Systems buckets for warm-starting.
- Purge mechanics: we can enforce TTL-based deletion at the object-store level for the RB dataset tag to implement the 60-day purge. The deletion job generates a deletion log (timestamp, object id, deletion hash) and emits a tombstone event we retain in an immutable audit topic for 30 days by default — we can extend that to 90 days if needed as part of the amendment.
- Forensics exception: we will support a ticketed, time-bound hold that flips an object tag to "forensics-hold" and automatically moves objects to a customer-scoped, encrypted-forensics bucket for up to 180 days. Access requires a signed SIR (security incident request) plus dual approval (Security lead + Customer contact). All accesses are logged to a separate immutable audit file.
- Subprocessors: confirm list and brief access scope:
  * QuantumCloud (quantumcloud.com) — primary object-store, has access to encrypted backups (no key access).
  * EdgeGPU Systems (edgegpu.net) — serving snapshot replication; ephemeral caches only but can receive warmed snapshots.
  * MetricsHub (metrics.example) — aggregated telemetry; does not store backups.

I'll attach a short runbook snippet and a sample purge log. Let me know if Riverbend requires the audit retention for deletion logs to exceed 90 days; we can propose 180 days for the immutable deletion audit if that eases compliance.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Attachment: purge_runbook_snippet.txt
